passages.note: House Third Reading vote page shows Dunn voting Y on final passage, 31-26 (not near-unanimous); he was a State Representative in this legislature in February 2022, so V5 option B applies.

passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted bill text (Chapter 99): single-subject registration/citizenship bill whose operative sections condition registration on documentary proof of citizenship, matching rung 5 clause for clause.
Bill overview page establishes the instrument's short title and enactment; Dunn is not on the sponsor list, so the vote is the act relied on.

rows.reasoning: Dunn voted Y on final House passage of HB 2492 (2022), a single-subject registration bill (31-26, so not near-unanimous), cast while he served in this legislature's House. Its operative text provides that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship", which is the rung requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote. The bill's weaker identity clauses (an identifying document for proof of location of residence, a driver licence or SSN number) sit beside that clause and do not displace it.
